name: balance-scales
title: Balance scales (equations)
tagline: Linear equation as a level two-pan balance of boxes and unit weights; derives the equation, the solution and same-to-both-sides steps for solving.
description: A linear equation drawn as a level two-pan balance: each pan carries a number of unknown-boxes (the coefficient) and unit weights (the constant), and the beam is level because the two sides are equal — the balance is the equals sign. You give each side as counts ({boxes, units}); the model derives the tiles and their layout, the equation string above the beam (e.g. "3x + 2 = 14"), the solved value of the unknown below it (reduced to a fraction when it is not whole), and — given an operation — the same-to-both-sides step as an overlay: "remove" strikes equal tiles from each pan ("− 2" or "− x"), "group" splits each pan into equal groups and highlights one ("÷ 3"). Built for solving one- and two-step equations and equations with unknowns on both sides, frame by frame, by keeping the balance level. v1 holds non-negative whole tiles and a level (true-equation) beam.
whenToUse: Reach for this to teach solving linear equations with the balance metaphor: representing ax + b = c (and unknowns on both sides) as weights on a balance, and solving by doing the same to both sides — removing equal amounts, and dividing/halving both sides. Write the equation as two sides of counts: 3x + 2 = 14 is left {boxes:3, units:2}, right {boxes:0, units:14}; 2x + 1 = x + 5 is left {boxes:2, units:1}, right {boxes:1, units:5}. The equation string and the solved value are computed — you never type them. Common configurations: solve (omit solution; the balance and equation are the question, and "Solve for x" goes in the block text); show the answer (add solution to print "x = 4", solution.highlight to amber it); ask for the answer (solution.occlude → "x = ?"); write the equation (show.equation:false, so the picture alone is the prompt "what equation does this balance show?"). This model is naturally staged — each stage does one operation to both pans. Build a solve as a sequence of frames: frame = the current equation, optionally with an operation overlay marking the step, then the next frame is the simplified equation. operation {type:"remove", units:2} strikes 2 unit weights from each pan (use boxes to strike x-boxes, e.g. {type:"remove", boxes:1} for unknowns-on-both-sides); operation {type:"group", groups:3} splits each pan into 3 equal groups and highlights one — the divide step. The base frame (no operation) must read as a sensible balance on its own (a slide opens on it). Cross-block convention: keep the unknown letter and the unit style the same across one lesson so pupils track one balance; keep each pan within a comfortable width (a couple of boxes plus a row or two of units) so a staged build does not resize between frames. Switch model when the teaching changes: for sequential operations on one number (a number going in, operations applied, a number out) use algebra/function-machine; for a part-whole / ratio bar or an equation as a segmented bar use number/bar-model; for expanding or factorising brackets use algebra/area-model. Synonyms a teacher might use: balance, balance scales, scales, weighing scales, balancing equations, solve the equation, do the same to both sides, isolate x, one-step / two-step equations, unknowns on both sides, inverse operations.
tags: do the same to both sides

equation.description: The equation the balance models, as its two pans. The beam is drawn level because the equation asserts the sides are equal — give an equation that has a solution (a side may be all boxes, all units, or both).

left.description: The LEFT pan. One pan of the balance. boxes is the coefficient of the unknown (the number of x-boxes); units is the constant (the number of unit weights). Side {boxes:3, units:2} reads 3x + 2; {boxes:0, units:14} reads 14; {boxes:1, units:0} reads x.

boxes.description: How many unknown-boxes sit on this pan — the coefficient of the unknown. 0 = no boxes on this side. Each box is drawn the same and labelled with the unknown letter.

units.description: The constant on this pan — the number of unit weights. A whole number ≤ 25 is drawn as that many small unit cubes (so "take 2 off both sides" is concrete); a larger or non-whole value is drawn as a single weight labelled with the number (see unitMode to force either).

right.description: The RIGHT pan. One pan of the balance. boxes is the coefficient of the unknown (the number of x-boxes); units is the constant (the number of unit weights). Side {boxes:3, units:2} reads 3x + 2; {boxes:0, units:14} reads 14; {boxes:1, units:0} reads x.

boxes.description: How many unknown-boxes sit on this pan — the coefficient of the unknown. 0 = no boxes on this side. Each box is drawn the same and labelled with the unknown letter.

units.description: The constant on this pan — the number of unit weights. A whole number ≤ 25 is drawn as that many small unit cubes (so "take 2 off both sides" is concrete); a larger or non-whole value is drawn as a single weight labelled with the number (see unitMode to force either).

unknown.description: The single lowercase letter the boxes represent. Default "x". Use the same letter across one lesson.

operation.description: An optional overlay showing the ONE step about to be done to BOTH pans — it annotates the current equation, it does not change it (author the next frame as the simplified equation). Omit for a plain balance.

type.description: "remove" strikes equal tiles from each pan (the subtract step) — set boxes and/or units to say how many of each. "group" splits each pan into equal groups and highlights one group (the divide/halve step) — set groups.

boxes.description: remove: how many x-boxes to strike from EACH pan (e.g. 1 to take an x off both sides). Ignored for "group". Default 0.

units.description: remove: how many unit weights to strike from EACH pan (e.g. 2 to take 2 off both sides). Ignored for "group". Default 0.

groups.description: group: the number of equal groups to split EACH pan into (e.g. 3 to divide both sides by 3); one group is highlighted as the result. Required for "group".

solution.description: Include this to print the solved value of the unknown beneath the balance (e.g. "x = 4", or a reduced fraction like "x = 3/2"). Omit it for a plain balance the pupil solves themselves. The value is computed from the two sides — you never type it.

occlude.description: Render the value as "?" ("x = ?") — the "what is the unknown?" hook. The balance and equation stay visible. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the solved value — answer emphasis. Default false.

equation.description: Show the derived equation string (e.g. "3x + 2 = 14") above the beam. Set false to ask "what equation does this balance show?" — the picture alone is then the prompt. Default true.

unitMode.description: How a pan's constant is drawn. Omit for auto: a whole number ≤ 25 becomes that many unit cubes (concrete for "remove 2"), anything larger or non-whole becomes a single labelled weight. "cubes" forces individual cubes; "weight" forces a single block labelled with the number (cleaner for big constants).

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
